matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After proposing a transformed equation, convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and verify that the equality holds; without this, you may accept an equation that is still false.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalizing the answer, compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation and confirm they are equal.
matchstick.example: Accepting the equation 'X = XI + I' without checking that 10 ≠ 12.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick retains its orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) when moved; you cannot rotate it to a different orientation, otherwise the resulting character may be invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When relocating a stick, keep its original orientation and ensure the destination character can accept that orientation.
matchstick.example: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical one, turning a V into an I.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single‑stick move may affect at most two distinct characters: the source loses the stick and the destination gains it; altering more characters makes the move invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During the move, track which characters lose or gain a stick and ensure the count does not exceed two.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from X to V and also adding it to a separate I, affecting three characters.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Only certain Roman‑numeral pairs can be changed by moving a single stick while keeping both characters valid (e.g., V↔X, I↔II↔III); attempting other changes yields invalid numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a numeral, consider the known single‑stick transformations before inventing a new shape.
matchstick.example: Trying to turn X into V by simply removing a diagonal, which leaves an invalid slash.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must be a single line beginning with the exact phrase ‘Correct version of the equation:’, otherwise the answer is not recognized.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer, prepend the required prefix and ensure no extra lines or text appear.
matchstick.example: Providing just 'XI = X + I' without the required prefix.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ creates a ‘+’; removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ yields a ‘‑’; neglecting this conversion may miss a valid solution.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains ‘+’ or ‘‑’, consider moving a vertical stick between them.
matchstick.example: Overlooking that turning ‘+’ into ‘‑’ by removing its vertical stick could make the equation true.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer from '+' to numeral (adds I)
matchstick.principle: Removing the vertical stick from a ‘+’ (turning it into ‘‑’) and adding that stick to a numeral that can accept an I (e.g., X → XI) yields a valid transformation; forgetting to change the ‘+’ leaves an invalid operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a ‘+’, try moving its vertical stick to a numeral that can grow by one.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from ‘+’ to X but leaving the ‘+’ unchanged, resulting in an invalid ‘+’.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via horizontal stick relocation
matchstick.principle: Removing one horizontal line from ‘=’ turns it into ‘‑’; adding a horizontal line to ‘‑’ turns it into ‘=’; failing to place the moved stick leaves an incomplete operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains ‘=’ or ‘‑’, consider moving a horizontal stick between them.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal from ‘=’ to make ‘‑’ but not adding it elsewhere, leaving the equation with a missing ‘=’.

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A V can be turned into an X (and vice versa) by moving a single diagonal stick within the same character; using this transformation correctly can adjust values by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a V or X appears and the arithmetic is off by 5, try repositioning a diagonal stick inside that character.
matchstick.example: Attempting to change V to X by adding a diagonal from elsewhere instead of moving the existing diagonal.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick transfer between numerals (I ↔ I)
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick (the I) from a numeral that contains an I character to another numeral that can accept an I (by appending it) yields a valid transformation, provided both source and destination remain valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains an I as a separate character within a multi‑character numeral (e.g., XI, XII) and another numeral that can be increased by adding an I (e.g., X, V), consider swapping the I by moving its stick.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from the I in ‘XI’ to the X on the other side, but leaving the source token empty, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on finding a plausible stick move and forgets to check whether the resulting Roman‑numeral equation is mathematically true.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the integer values of both sides after any proposed transformation and confirm the equality before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When moving a stick, the model may produce a character that does not correspond to any Roman numeral or operator (e.g., a slash from X).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Refer to the list of allowed single‑stick transformations and ensure each affected character remains a recognized numeral or operator.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may change an operator into a shape that is not a valid operator (e.g., turning ‘+’ into a shape that is neither ‘+’, ‘‑’, nor ‘=’).
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving sticks involving operators, restrict changes to the known conversions: ‘+’↔‘‑’ via vertical sticks, ‘=’↔‘‑’ via horizontal sticks.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a source character but does not attach it to any destination, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Every stick relocation must specify both a source character (which loses the stick) and a destination character (which gains it).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model outputs the transformed equation without the required prefix line or with extra text, causing the scorer to miss the answer.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: End the response with a single line exactly: ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’.
